features.name: App shell and sidebar nav
features.notes: Eleven routes in four sections, re-rendered by renderSidebar() on every route change. Fewer than eleven links means a ROUTES entry was dropped or renderSidebar threw before finishing, which also leaves the previous view on screen.

features.name: Dashboard: Overview tab
features.notes: The default route when the hash is empty. Five tabs (Overview, Leagues, Trajectory, Market, Cornerstones) plus the command cards. An empty cmd-grid means the leagues data failed to load, and every other view will be thin too.

features.name: Dashboard: Leagues tab and positional heatmap
features.notes: One card and one heatmap row per league (3 leagues for 2026). A missing row is a league whose roster failed to resolve, not a styling problem.

features.name: Dashboard: Trajectory tab
features.notes: Present value vs future value per league plus the multi-year grid. The PV/FV bar width is inline-styled, so a NaN collapses the bar while the row still renders.

features.name: Dashboard: Market movers tab
features.notes: Risers and fallers from the KTC snapshot. Empty means ktc.js loaded but the previous snapshot is missing, so every delta computed as zero and got filtered out.

features.name: Dashboard: Cornerstones tab
features.notes: The players you hold across leagues, tier-chipped. Rows are the intersection of rosters and rankings, so a rankings file rename empties this table with no error.

features.name: My Leagues table
features.notes: One row per tracked league (4 Sleeper plus 1 ESPN for 2026). A different count means generated league data drifted and downstream views are stale.

features.name: League detail: standings
features.notes: Reached by clicking a league row, which is the path a person actually uses. Strength ranks stay fixed while rows sort. Schedule difficulty exposes gross starter-bye production missing from the opponents this team will face.

features.name: League standings: sensible sort order

features.name: League detail: Players tab
features.notes: Every rostered player in the league, with filters. This replaced the old All Players route, so it is the only full list left; a short table means the Sleeper roster payload truncated.

A Gibbs ROS column renders only when he publishes a rest-of-season board, so the header count is a floor, not an equality.

features.name: Roster view: team blueprint

features.name: Action Center to-do list

features.name: Trade Calculator
features.notes: Two side cards, player search and an on-demand championship odds simulation. The fairness verdict only appears once both piles have something, so the empty state is correct.

Partner rows include the Sleeper username when available. Historical picks join season, round and stable original-owner user ID to the completed rookie draft, then show the exact slot and player selected.

features.name: Player Projections tables
features.notes: Blended PrizePicks / Sleeper projections, offense and defense in separate tables (~180 rows). A sharp drop means one source file failed to parse and the blend silently fell back to a single source.

features.name: Strength of Schedule grid
features.assert: document.querySelectorAll('#main table.data tbody tr').length === 32 && document.querySelectorAll('#main .team-chip').length >= 32 && document.querySelectorAll('#main .sos-position-tabs button[aria-pressed]').length === 4 && document.querySelector('#main .page-sub').textContent.includes('Week 1')

features.name: Draft Room entry form
features.notes: Best-available board for a Sleeper draft URL. Without a draft id it shows the paste form, the only state reachable offline; the live board needs the Sleeper API and is deliberately not verified here.

features.name: My Rankings editable board
features.notes: Your saved order seeded from Gibbs full-PPR (~527 rows), drag-reorderable by the grip. Losing the grips makes the board read-only with no error shown.

features.name: Framework (the dynasty rules)
features.notes: The rule set every roster evaluation cites, rendered from strategy.js. An empty table means the roster views still render but with no reasoning behind them.

features.name: Sources: analyst toggles
features.notes: Which analysts feed the aggregate, with per-video toggles written to localStorage. A lost switch silently freezes the aggregate at its last state.

features.name: About: methodology table
features.notes: How rankings and team strength are computed. This is the page that keeps the numbers honest, so an empty table is a real regression, not a cosmetic one.

features.name: Cmd+K command palette
features.notes: The front door: routes, leagues, rosters and ranked players are all searchable here, plus the two static Gibbs pages. Zero rows means rankIndex() threw while building the index, leaving an overlay you can only escape with Esc.

features.name: Mobile nav toggle
features.notes: The hamburger at phone widths; it sets body.nav-open and shows the scrim. Verified at 420px because the button is display:none on desktop, which is why this feature carries its own viewport. route() clears nav-open on every navigation, so a sidebar stuck open after a click is that line being lost.

features.name: Boot renders a view, not the error branch
features.notes: route() catches render errors and prints them into a .empty div, so a thrown view looks like an empty page rather than a crash. This asserts that branch was not taken; failOnConsoleError covers the rest.

features.name: League Transactions: FAAB archetype cost panel
features.notes: Box plots use three decision-time dimensions: situation, position and NFL experience. Post-claim production is excluded because it was unknown when the bid was made. Every number is priced per league because budgets and local markets differ.

features.name: League FAAB: drill into archetype claim history
features.assert: (() => { const d = document.querySelector('#main .faab-history[open]'); return !!d && Number(d.querySelector('.faab-n').textContent.replace('n=', '')) === d.querySelectorAll('tbody tr').length; })()
features.notes: Each league-specific archetype row opens its paid claim history. Visible row count must equal displayed n. $0 adds stay in recommendation samples and zero-share, not paid-history n.

features.name: League: FAAB tab beside Standings / Players / Transactions
features.notes: FAAB is a league view like the others. It previously existed only at the top of the Transactions feed and inside a collapsed panel on the Action Center, which read as unimplemented three separate times. Trade Lab moved into this same bar and links out to its own #trade route rather than being re-implemented as a tab body. Note validTabs in viewLeague gates the sub-route: a tab present in the bar but absent from that list silently falls back to standings. Also asserts the week's waiver board, which carries the recommended bid range per candidate. Note the tab guard reads formats[fmt].situation.length: formats[fmt] is an object keyed by dimension, and an array .length check there silently removes the tab.

features.name: Player card: team context blocks (tendencies, QB, turnover)
features.notes: The blocks contextBlock() builds from site/data/context.js: tendencies, the QB line, turnover, the new-team transition and career availability. Each reads a DIFFERENT derived file whose newest season is a different year, and a missing key does not throw, it renders nothing. On 2026-09-17 turnover moved to 2026 while qb_changes still topped out at 2025, a shared latest-season lookup missed, and all 32 teams silently lost the QB line while every other block and every other feature stayed green. So the markers are asserted BY NAME, not by a block count: .qb-line for the QB, .turn-list for turnover, .availability for career health (whose builder is the one the season_window guard protects). Mutation-checked by stripping the 32 qb objects out of context.js, which fails this case and nothing else. Lives behind the card's Context tab since the Value/Production/Context shell landed, so the path clicks that tab first; the element renders either way but is display:none until then.

features.name: Player card: career PPG chart
features.notes: Career chart in KTC's grammar: filled area, high and low labelled, current value called out, signed delta. Replaced a 168x36 teal polyline with no axis, no years and no values. The KTC tab only appears once site/data/build_ktc_history.py has written ktc-history.js, so the tab bar is optional and a single series must still draw. Unit test: site/js/career-chart.test.js. UPDATE 2026-09-17: the KTC series was promoted out of this chart into ktcValueChart(), which opens the Value tab with its own 3mo/1yr/All range control and a signed change callout. This chart is points-per-game only now, so careerChart renders it with no tab strip at all, which is why the tab clause here is written to accept zero .cchart-tabs. The chart also now lives inside the hidden Production panel, so the assertion must not depend on visibility.

features.name: Player card: this week's projection, opponent and DvP
features.notes: Answers the weekly start-sit question the card previously answered with a season projection. Reads WEEKLY_RANKINGS for the per-week projection and sos-grid.js for defense-vs-position, which index.html had been loading unread. A bye renders as a bye rather than a zero, and an IDP shows the opponent without a DvP rank because the grid covers QB/RB/WR/TE only. Runs LAST of the three features that share the Cmd+K player-card path: an open modal swallows the next feature's Control+k, so inserting this one first made team-context time out waiting for .qb-line.

features.name: Player card: six-cell number band
features.notes: The six figures the card is read for, in one fixed order, replacing two stacked rows of chips that wrapped differently on every player. Gibbs is used deliberately: he is ranked AND has an offense projection, so all six cells are reachable and a missing one is a real defect. Six is a ceiling, not a floor, for other players: Value and Tier need a ranking, Value rank and Proj pts come from mispricingIndex() which is built from OFFENSE_PROJ.offense only (so an IDP has neither), and Cooper Rush correctly renders one cell. The .price-line clause is the anti-duplication check: that class was the old chip row, and it must stay gone or every number prints twice. Browser matrix: site/_playercard_check.py.

features.name: Player card: Value / Production / Context tabs
features.notes: Seventeen reference blocks behind three tabs, reusing .tab-bar / .tab so the card inherits the 44px touch target rather than growing a second tab component. Exactly one panel visible is the load-bearing assertion: the panels are siblings and a stale hidden flag shows two at once. The last clause pins the judge's ordering decision, that the KTC value chart opens the default Value tab instead of sitting behind a points-per-game tab inside historyBlock. A group with no surviving blocks drops its own tab, so an unranked player with no KTC history gets two tabs, not three with one blank; that case is covered in site/_playercard_check.py rather than here, because this feature asserts the full-data shape.

features.name: Action Center: user-maintained target / trade-block board
features.notes: Replaced a computed suggestion queue that was usually empty and otherwise guessed at intent it cannot see. Driven by two marks the manager sets: star a player NOT on his roster (target) or flag one of his own (trade block), stored per league in localStorage under tier-sheet-marks-v1 because wanting a man in yuH is a different plan from wanting him in taco. Toggles live on the player card and in the league Players list; note that list renders through the name cell near app.js:3075, NOT weeklyNameCell, which is why an earlier pass added the button and nothing appeared.

features.name: IDP league: which offenses feed defenders
features.assert: (() => { const cards=[...document.querySelectorAll('#main .card')]; const c=cards.find(x=>x.textContent.includes('IDP matchups')); if(!c) return false; const rows=c.querySelectorAll('tbody tr'); const D=window.IDP_DVP; const opp=[...c.querySelectorAll('tbody tr')].filter(r=>!r.textContent.includes('bye or not scheduled')).length; return rows.length === Object.keys(D.offenses).length && opp >= 20; })()
features.notes: The mirror of the offense SOS grid, and only rendered for an IDP league (idpMatchupBlock returns null otherwise, so the other four leagues are unaffected). Two clauses carry weight: the row count must match the payload so a partial build is visible, and at least 20 rows must resolve a week-N opponent. That second one is the bug this test exists for: the opponent lookup first read SOS_GRID.teams, which is a flat list of team codes with its grid keyed by POSITION, and then window.SOS, which does not exist. The schedule is window.TEAM_SOS.teams[abbr].schedule. Both wrong versions rendered a full, plausible table with every opponent cell reading 'bye or not scheduled'.

features.name: Weekly table: Gibbs rest-of-season rank from his X posts
features.assert: (() => { const g = window.GIBBS_ROS; if (!g) return false; const heads=[...document.querySelectorAll('table.weekly-rankings-table thead th')].map(h=>h.textContent.replace(/[↑↓]/g,'').trim().toUpperCase()); const i=heads.indexOf('GIBBS X'); if(i<0) return false; const ranked=new Set(); for(const rows of Object.values(g.positions)) for(const r of rows) if(r.sleeperId) ranked.add(String(r.sleeperId)); const cells=[...document.querySelectorAll('table.weekly-rankings-table tbody tr')].map(tr=>tr.children[i]?.textContent.trim()).filter(t=>t && t!=='·'); return ranked.size >= 140 && cells.length >= 100 && /^(RB|WR|QB|TE)\d+/.test(cells[0]); })()
features.notes: His rest-of-season positional board, captured from his own X posts and transcribed by two independent readers before it was allowed into the repo (WR agreed 77 of 77, RB 69 of 70, the split being the spelling of Jeremiyah Love). Separate from the JACOB_GIBBS_RANKINGS overall draft board and from the FantasyPros-sourced 'Gibbs ROS' column beside it: FantasyPros lagged this by a day at capture and never carries his positional ROS lists at all. The assert checks the payload and the DOM together so a stale or empty gibbs-ros.js cannot pass as a rendered column. Only RB and WR are populated because those are the only boards he posted; QBs showing a dot rather than a number is correct, not a gap. HALF-PPR, which is what he publishes, while all three leagues are full PPR, so the cell shows HIS rank and never a rescored one.

ignoreReason: Draft Room calls the live Sleeper API on mount to list your 2026 drafts. That call is the one deliberately-online surface in an otherwise file:// app, so it fails in a headless offline run. Scoped to the single host: any other failed request still fails the gate.
